What degraded

  • THE DECK SHIPPED UNDER THE BAR. Panel median 6.968 against an 8.0 threshold, 1.032 under, at the five round cap with no hard fail outstanding. Round 5's three judges scored 6.938, 7.156 and 7.042 and every one refused on the NUMBER rather than on a fault, each saying so in as many words.
  • tx-2026-0120 could not be re-verified. www.dhs.gov answered 403 to every client this run had, including a plain fetch of robots.txt itself, which is an edge block rather than a robots decision. The item keeps its previous stamp and carries a dated note naming what is unconfirmed.
  • Three sources on the El Paso and Carrollton story refused: transparency.flocksafety.com 403, cityofcarrollton.com 403, and Carrollton's CivicClerk API 404. That story was set aside on dedupe_check rather than on access, so nothing was lost to it.
  • The Supabase scanner ceiling query did not run. No connector is attached in this session.
  • Frame 1 still reads as a wireframe, frame 7 as a thicket rather than a filing box, frame 4's tank does not read as a cylinder, and frame 9's exterior payoff does not arrive. Each is a frame redraw named by a judge and each is next run work, because this run had already turned one late cheap improvement into a hard fail.
  • The deck carries no Texas place below the state. Brazos County is the drawn world and reaches no frame. The drawing law forbids a county sign and nothing forbade the copy, so this is a cost the run took rather than a rule it obeyed.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it Three queries. Three counts. No total., paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

Aimed at small systems. Texas has 4,749.

Those are the active community water systems on the EPA's record. 3,579 of them serve fewer than 3,301 people. A separate count puts 87 over 50,000.

The National Science Foundation made a standard grant to the Texas A&M Engineering Experiment Station on September 9th. Work began September 15th. The award expires August 31st, 2029. The abstract's first stated direction is predictive digital twins for small and mid-sized systems.

Utility practice often relies on monitoring, historical records and reactive emergency protocols. That is a complete account of what already happened. The abstract says the project can support earlier warning of how a local anomaly escalates. No deployment is recorded.

TCEQ sends a resident to their own system's annual drinking water quality report. Which of those 3,579 ever gets a twin?

#TexasWater #TCEQ #TexasAM

"Eleven docket items carry last_verified 2026-09-20. Eight were due on the worklist, three were admitted today. Two items that reverify.py reported MISSING were not missing: tx-2026-0156 and tx-2026-0165 both failed on a curly apostrophe against a straight one, and the run downloaded the PDF and the page and confirmed every claim verbatim before stamping either. The promote gate refused four of five admission candidates on the first pass and was right every time, so the seed was repaired at source rather than the gate loosened. The best story of the day was refused: the El Paso and Carrollton licence plate reader split returned LIKELY REPEAT at 0.74 against carousel no. 12, 21 days back, and the full ledger entry was read rather than its title. The El Paso decision is in the record as tx-2026-0174 either way."
